quote.after:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let causal
curves be those of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]].

**(a) Convergent ends are extendible.** Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the general absolutely continuous endpoint argument in this clause. Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a future
causal curve and suppose $b:=\sup I<\infty$ and $\gamma(t)\to x\in M$ as
$t\to\sup I$. Then there is $\varepsilon>0$ and a future causal curve
$\tilde\gamma$ defined on $I\cup[b,b+\varepsilon)$ whose restriction to $I$
is $\gamma$. Consequently a future-inextendible causal curve whose domain is
bounded above does not converge at its upper end, and the dual statement
holds at the past end.

**(b) Maximal geodesics have no limit.** Let $(p,v)\in TM$ with $v\ne0$ and
let $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ be the unique maximal geodesic with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$, as supplied by
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a). Then
$\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ does not converge to any point of $M$ as $t\to\sup I_{p,v}$
or as $t\to\inf I_{p,v}$ (where convergence at an infinite end means
convergence as $t\to+\infty$ or $t\to-\infty$ respectively).

**(c) Segments lie on inextendible causal curves.** Let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to M$
with $t_0<t_1$ be a future causal curve, or a past causal curve. Then there
is an inextendible causal curve $\hat\gamma:J\to M$ (same direction as
$\gamma$ in the case at hand) and a strictly increasing affine map
$\rho:[t_0,t_1]\to J$ with $\hat\gamma\circ\rho=\gamma$. In particular, any
two distinct points $p,q\in M$ with $p\le q$ and $p\ne q$ lie on a common
inextendible causal curve, and likewise for the past relation.

**(d) Cauchy sets are acausal.** Every Cauchy set of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c) is acausal in
the sense of clause (b) of that definition.

after.claim: (The cone function.) For $q\in A$ write $v:=q-p'$, so $v=(v^0,v_{\mathrm{vec}})$ and $Q(q):=-\eta(v,v)=(v^0)^2-|v_{\mathrm{vec}}|^2$. By [L1], $Q(q)>0$ exactly when $v$ is timelike, $Q(q)=0$ exactly when $v$ is null (or zero), and the sign of $v^0$ together with [L1] identifies the future and past sides: $\{Q>0,v^0>0\}$ is the chronological future $I^+(p')$ of the flat model and $\{Q>0,v^0<0\}$ its chronological past.

(The gradient of $Q$.) In the chart components, $dQ=2v^0\,dx^0-2\sum_iv^i\,dx^i$, and the vector field $W:=-2v^0\partial_0-2\sum_iv^i\partial_i$ satisfies $\eta(W,w)=2v^0w^0-2\sum_iv^iw^i=dQ(w)$ for all $w$, so $\nabla Q=W=-2v$ by [L4]. Consequently $\nabla Q$ is past-directed timelike exactly on $\{Q>0,v^0>0\}$, namely on $I^+(p')$, and it vanishes nowhere on the zero set of $Q$ except at the vertex $q=p'$.

(The smoothed bump is smooth and its gradient is past timelike where it is positive.) Let $f:=\varphi\circ Q$. Since $Q$ is smooth and $\varphi$ is smooth with all derivatives vanishing at $0$, the composition is smooth at the vertex and on the rest of the zero set; it is constant $0$ where $Q\le0$ and smooth where $Q>0$ [L3]. Moreover $f\ge0$ and $f>0$ exactly on $I^+(p')$ by step 1.1. Where $f>0$ one has $
abla f=\varphi'(Q)
abla Q$ by the chain rule; since $Q>0$ there and $\varphi'(Q)= rac{1}{Q^2}e^{-1/Q}>0$, the gradient $
abla f$ is a positive multiple of the past-directed timelike $
abla Q$ of step 2.1, hence is past timelike on $\{f>0\}$.

(The normalized bump.) Since $p-p'=(\delta,0,0,0)$ is future timelike, $Q(p)=\delta^2>0$ and $f(p)=\varphi(\delta^2)>0$; hence $h_p:=\chi f/f(p)$ is defined for every smooth $\chi:A\to[0,1]$ with compact support. Taking $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $p$ gives $h_p(p)=1$ and, by continuity, $\{h_p>1/2\}$ containing a neighborhood of $p$; taking $\operatorname{supp}\chi$ compact gives $h_p$ compact support. On any prescribed compact subset $K$ of $I^+(p')$ on which $\chi=1$, one has $h_p=f/f(p)$ and $\nabla h_p=\nabla f/f(p)$, which is past timelike by step 3.1; in particular, for the truncated sets $\{x^0\le b\}\cap K$ of the cone-bump lemma the same computation gives clause (c) of [[lem-gr-cone-bump-functions]] in this explicit model.

(Summary.) The explicit data $(Q,f,h_p)$ realise the cone-bump lemma at $p'$ in the flat model: $Q$ is the exponential cone function, $f$ the smoothing of the indicator of the chronological future of $p'$, and $h_p$ the normalized compactly supported bump with $h_p(p)=1$ and past-timelike gradient where it is positive.
